title: Monetary Policy Report—July 2025
summary: The Bank of Canada held its overnight rate target steady at 2.75% (Bank Rate at 3%, deposit rate at 2.70%) as US tariffs and trade uncertainty weighed on economic activity. Canadian growth has slowed considerably due to the trade conflict but is showing resilience, while headline inflation remains near the 2% target with underlying inflation elevated at approximately 2.5%.
key_points: Bank of Canada maintained overnight rate target at 2.75% (Bank Rate 3%, deposit rate 2.70%)
Canadian economic activity has slowed considerably due to the trade conflict but is showing signs of resilience
Headline inflation near 2%, but underlying inflation has risen to about 2.5%
US tariffs are significantly higher than at the start of 2025 and US trade policy remains unpredictable
Global growth has slowed since the start of 2025 amid ongoing shifts in US trade policy
Governing Council: Tiff Macklem (Governor), Carolyn Rogers (Senior Deputy Governor), Toni Gravelle, Sharon Kozicki, Nicolas Vincent, Rhys Mendes, Michelle Alexopoulos
why_it_matters: This quarterly monetary policy report provides the Bank of Canada's comprehensive assessment of economic conditions and outlook. The hold at 2.75% reflects the delicate balance between supporting a slowing economy amid trade uncertainty while monitoring rising underlying inflation pressures. Market participants watch these reports closely for signals on the rate path and how the Bank is interpreting tariff impacts on the Canadian economy.
macro_context: US tariff escalation and trade policy unpredictability are the primary catalysts weighing on Canadian economic activity. While the global economy has remained resilient despite the highest US tariff levels in decades, Canada faces specific headwinds from trade disruption. The Bank's 2% inflation target remains within reach on a headline basis, though underlying price pressures have increased, creating a nuanced policy environment.
